groups.reason: Peer actions, navigation controls, toolbar controls and choice actions use the single approved action-group gap. This replaces legacy per-page 5–10px variants without changing hit-target ownership.
Repeated list/grid items, weekday choices and compact evidence stacks use the single approved list gap.
Record/search/count/feedback form groups and selectable form options use the single approved form-field group gap.
Labels, values, metadata, compact copy and nested status facts use the approved tight field gap rather than page-specific micro values.
Row-level icon, copy, status and metadata arrangements use the approved row-content gap across tasks, records, reviews, growth and settings.
Page-level content stacks, editor panels, analysis sections and dialog content groups use the approved spacing between peer groups.
Content within a single analysis, evidence, entity, diary or growth section uses the approved component-title/content spacing.
Wide analysis sections intentionally counter the 20px page gutter and now derive that offset from the same spacing step.
Analysis bands counter the roomy 16px content inset while retaining zero vertical margin.
Narrow-screen analysis bands counter the 12px responsive page inset through the same spacing step.
Evidence rows and disclosure controls use compact vertical and regular horizontal spacing from the shared scale.
Compact toolbar, action row and record option insets retain their vertical/horizontal roles using the shared scale.
Page and editor top insets share the 16px minimum while continuing to respect the device safe area.
Network and date controls retain tight vertical and compact horizontal insets through the shared scale.
Small alignment corrections for tabs and scope details derive from the same tight spacing step.
Inline detail controls retain tight vertical spacing and zero horizontal inset.
Day content and habit-analysis hero retain top-only tight spacing.
Habit overview and its empty state use the same expanded vertical and large horizontal content inset.
Preview action and growth-stat pairs share compact row and roomy column spacing.
Quick-task input retains compact vertical and micro horizontal inset.
Feedback actions retain a roomy minimum bottom inset while respecting the device safe area.
Review decision rows retain compact vertical and zero horizontal inset.
Event and confirmation tags use micro vertical and compact horizontal inset.
Journal sheet retains regular vertical and zero horizontal inset.
Today focus list retains compact top, page-gutter sides and regular bottom inset.
Habit week card uses regular vertical and compact horizontal inset.
Record save-state alignment retains its compact negative top, micro sides and zero bottom margin.
Habit comparison heading keeps regular top, roomy sides and compact bottom inset.
Habit comparison copy uses tight row and regular column spacing.
Analysis summary grid uses roomy vertical and regular horizontal inset.
The parallel settings heading was removed; the shared list section now owns heading-to-content spacing.
AI settings title retains a large top-only inset.
Day navigation retains a compact minimum bottom inset while respecting the safe area.
Goal detail link counter-aligns the roomy list inset through the same shared spacing step.
Secondary day pages retain a large minimum bottom inset while respecting the safe area.
Day overview facts retain compact top, zero sides and tight bottom inset.
Day overview fact controls use regular vertical and roomy horizontal inset.
Floating task action retains roomy top, zero right, tight bottom and automatic left alignment.
Full-screen editor content uses expanded top/bottom insets and the shared page gutter while respecting the safe area.
Analysis section uses large vertical and zero horizontal inset.
Analysis summary uses large vertical and roomy horizontal inset.
Diary feed retains bottom-only large inset.
Habit detail hero uses compact top, zero sides and large bottom inset.
Remaining single-value micro spacing declarations use the existing 2px spacing step; direction and component ownership remain unchanged.
The compact analysis-page top inset uses the existing tight spacing step.
Remaining single-value compact gaps and insets use the existing 8px spacing step. This includes form/evidence internals, not artwork dimensions.
The analysis page's compact responsive horizontal inset uses the existing regular spacing step.
The narrow record-page gutter uses the existing roomy spacing step.
Large section separation and wide responsive page gutters use the existing 20px spacing step; media-specific declarations retain their original contexts.

Calendar weekday and date grids, activity dots and compact monthly meters use calendar-specific square/cell geometry and responsive offsets. These values maintain seven equal columns and distinguish date evidence; they are not list rows, form fields or general section spacing. The surrounding page shell and preview surfaces are excluded from this exception.

Heat cells, progress/momentum tracks, weekday charts and their labels need chart-specific square sizes, bar thicknesses and alignment offsets. They remain inside the shared analysis page and typography shells but cannot use list-row or button geometry without breaking the visualization. Form weekday pickers are deliberately excluded.

Pixel artwork, character hit regions, portrait framing and companion stages use asset-specific geometry and optical alignment. They are not ordinary list, form or page-shell components; consolidating them into control tokens would distort the approved character assets. Their selectors remain explicitly inventoried for later asset-specific review.

Semantic assets, badge marks and their containing canvases have context-specific optical sizes. These declarations describe image/mark rendering rather than the geometry of a list row or control; a single control-size token would make small inline icons and large evidence badges visually incorrect. Repeated width/height pairs stay together and remain audited as one optical-size category.
Content surfaces, grouped rows, diary attachments and feedback choice surfaces share the approved surface corner. These existing 8px corners are not artwork curvature or circular status markers.
Status chips and filled progress tracks intentionally use pill ends, separate from rectangular content surfaces.
Date/text input and stage toggle control outlines use the shared control corner, not the surface corner.
Full-screen editor, feedback shell and fixed submit strip follow the same responsive page-width ceiling rather than separate 480px widths.
The maximum width of the editor and feedback shell belongs to the shared page-width ceiling.
First row rounds only the top corners of the same grouped surface.
Last row rounds only the bottom corners of the same grouped surface.

Reviewed compact internal content spacing: icon/copy, status facts, preview contents and repeated chart labels use the existing compact spacing step. This is internal layout, not spacing between page sections or between list rows.
Assessment choice actions, quick-add input/action and task heading actions use the independent action-group spacing, not a section-title gap.
Compact inset for avatar choice, inline update notice, goal-link control and local image preview. They use the compact inset step rather than a page gutter.

Local content separation/inset within disclosures, evidence blocks, action details and attachment metadata uses the compact spacing step. Media conditions and property sides remain unchanged; outer section spacing continues to be owned by the shared page/section layer.

Reviewed regular internal content groups: return/notice rows, evidence and review sections, metadata and action/navigation strips share the regular spacing step. These legacy fallback declarations retain their cascade; public section/list contracts remain authoritative.

Regular control/content inset shared by compact buttons, closeout/assessment/revision content, evidence, notices, task context and habit comparison rows; not the page gutter or approved list horizontal padding.
Regular local separation between content and its follow-up/details; keep direction and conditional selector intact. Shared page/section containers still override obsolete outer margins.

Tight label/metadata separation and compact horizontal control inset use the shared tight spacing step. The selected properties are spacing only; 4px chart heights and decorative geometry are excluded.
Micro spacing between metadata, status facts and compact icon labels uses the smallest shared spacing step; excludes border widths, pixel art and heatmap cell geometry.

Roomy content inset/separation for journal sections, review groups, full editor groups, summary panels and record rows uses the shared roomy spacing step. Page-level group and typography ownership is unchanged.

Large container inset or separation for dialog content, fallback notice and calendar/overview blocks uses the existing large spacing step. Page gutters are independently controlled by --ui-page-padding.
Expanded separation between assessment modes and between large habit summary/chart groups uses the existing expanded spacing step.

Reviewed interactive controls: skip link, icon/text actions, avatar choices, disclosure summaries, form controls, task actions, calendar navigation and editor back controls all reserve the shared minimum touch target. This is hit-area geometry, not the smaller visible button height; artwork and noninteractive statistics with coincidentally equal dimensions are excluded.
